question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(\mu ,{5}^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(-0.8\mu <X<2.8\mu )=0.7458,$ find $\mu ,$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.0\,$ | $\,0.8485\,$ | $\,0.8508\,$ | $\,0.8531\,$ |
| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8708\,$ | $\,0.8729\,$ | $\,0.8749\,$ |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8907\,$ | $\,0.8925\,$ | $\,0.8944\,$ |

*Hint: Note that the interval $-0.8\mu <X<2.8\mu $ is symmetric about the mean $\mu .$*
question.worked_solution:
Note that we can write the given probability as

$$
P(\mu -1.8\mu <X<\mu +1.8\mu )=0.7458,
$$

which tells us that the interval $-0.8\mu <X<2.8\mu $ is symmetric about the mean $\mu .$

First, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\mu -1.8\mu <X<\mu +1.8\mu ) & =0.7458 \\ 2P(\mu <X<\mu +1.8\mu ) & =0.7458 \\ P(\mu <X<2.8\mu ) & =0.3729 \\ P(X<2.8\mu )-P(X<\mu ) & =0.3729 \\ P(X<2.8\mu )-0.5 & =0.3729 \\ P(X<2.8\mu ) & =0.8729 \\ P(X\le 2.8\mu ) & =0.8729\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 2.8\mu ) & =0.8729 \\ P(Z\le \frac{2.8\mu -\mu }{5}) & =0.8729 \\ Φ(\frac{1.8\mu }{5}) & =0.8729 \\ \frac{1.8\mu }{5} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.8729)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(1.14)=0.8729\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.8729)=1.14.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1.8\mu }{5} & =1.14 \\ 1.8\mu  & =5.7 \\ \mu  & ≈3.166\,67 \\ \mu  & ≈3.17.\end{aligned}
$$
